response.sql: SELECT L.ID, AVG(L.UA) AS avg_UA, AVG(L.HCT) AS avg_HCT FROM Laboratory L WHERE L.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(RA) <> '' AND RA <> '-') GROUP BY L.ID ORDER BY (AVG(L.HCT) IS NULL), AVG(L.HCT) DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: A patient qualifies if any of their lab rows has an RA that is non-NULL, not blank, and not '-'; values such as '+-' or '+' count as 'other than -'. A blank RA is treated as not recorded.
Once a patient qualifies, the averages are taken over all of that patient's lab rows, including rows where RA is '-' or missing, as the request says 'across all their lab records'.
Ties in average hematocrit are not broken in any defined way.

alternatives.interpretation: Averages are computed only over the lab rows whose RA is recorded and not '-', rather than over all of the patient's lab rows.
alternatives.sql: SELECT ID, AVG(UA) AS avg_UA, AVG(HCT) AS avg_HCT FROM Laboratory WHERE RA IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(RA) <> '' AND RA <> '-' GROUP BY ID ORDER BY (AVG(HCT) IS NULL), AVG(HCT) DESC LIMIT 10
